title: Page Builder Owed Items
eyebrow: Design for approval (parent issue #419) · nothing built yet
approval: Design approved: page builder owed items

short.lead: The page builder (make_page.py) let the build plan for the usage limit handoff go out with three change rows that read "null" and with no row naming its files. This change makes the builder refuse any page until everything that kind of page owes is filled in. The refusal lists every missing item at once, each named by its place on the page, so one fix pass clears it.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it adds and what it needs from you.
items: No page lets an empty field through (#420)

Every field the template prints as text is checked: the title, the opening paragraph, what each step creates and what it needs from you, each change row's one-line summary and its detail, each choice and every wrap-up field. A field that is missing, blank, or the word "null" or "undefined" is owed. Optional parts, such as a before-and-after pair or a picture, may still be left out.

A "Design approved:" page needs at least one change row, at least one row marked Kept (stays as it is) or Changed (or a sentence saying nothing like it exists today), and on every New row its three lines: what exists today, what the change creates, and how it affects you, and a suggested option with its reason on every choice.
What a build plan page owes (#422)

A "Build plan approved:" page needs a file list on every New and Changed row (the file's path, the estimated lines added and removed, and at least one sentence in plain words saying what changes in it), an issue number on every step, and the files named in the wrap-up's "What's changing". This is the gap the handoff plan slipped through.

A "QA passed:" page needs a list of the files git shows as changed, with at least one file, at least one "Still unverified" entry or a line saying nothing is left, and on every change row, the issue number it closes and the steps you follow to check it. It waits for the QA evidence work (issue #389) to merge, and does not alter that work.
Nothing from you; this step starts after #389 merges.
Tests, docs, version and a real run (#424)

Each owed item gets a test case in scripts/checks/make_page.py written before the code it tests. The broken version of the handoff plan (commit b7a1c13) must be refused, with its bad rows named, and the fixed version (commit a5c22c6) must build. This step also updates the docs and the plugin version, and ends with a real run of the builder.
Where the owed lists live, what happens to the older pages that would now fail, whether the after-build check also reads the page for "null", and how strict the build plan file rule is.
Your answers to the four choices.

changes: keep
The four refusals the builder already makes (make_page.py)
A reserved colour, a visual change with no picture, a wrong approval phrase, and missing QA fields.
These stay as they are. The new checks run beside them; the difference is that the new ones collect every problem before stopping, instead of stopping at the first.
chg
The build step (make_page.py, build)
Collects every owed item for the page's kind, then refuses once with the whole list.
Builds a page with "null" in three rows.
Refuses, naming each empty row and each row with no files.
A refusal line reads like: Changes row 3 "Approval reading": the detail is empty. The page kind comes from the approval phrase, which the builder already reads.
new
The owed lists
One list per page kind (proposal, build plan, QA) of what that page must fill in.
Choice 1 ("Where should the owed lists live?") decides where they live. Either way, the lists are the single place that says what a page owes, so the refusal and the docs read from the same source.
Nothing says what a page owes; only four narrow refusals exist.
A written list per page kind that the builder checks.
A page with a gap never reaches you; the builder sends it back to me first.
chg
The after-build visual check (make_page.py, visual_check)
Only if you pick it in choice 3 (whether the visual check also searches for "null" and "undefined"): also reads the rendered page for the words "null" and "undefined".
Looks for script errors, sideways overflow and clipped cards.
Also refuses a page whose visible text says "null" or "undefined".
This catches a gap the owed lists miss, such as a template field nobody listed yet. It runs in the browser check that already opens every card.
choices: where
Where should the owed lists live?
A
Inside make_page.py
Beside the four refusals that already live there; one file to read and test.
B
A data file beside the template
Separate from the code, but a second file that has to stay in step with the template's fields.
The other refusals are already Python in make_page.py, and the lists need code anyway (an issue-number pattern, a file-entry shape), so a data file would only move half of each rule.
old
19 of the 54 older proposal, build plan and QA pages in docs/plans/ would now be refused (13 build plans have rows with no files). What happens to them?
A
Leave them
The check runs only when a page is built, so the old pages stay as they are and are never rebuilt by accident.
B
Rebuild all 19
Fills in every gap; costs a page-by-page pass over finished features.
C
Rebuild only pages whose feature is still open
Fixes what you may still act on; leaves the finished history alone.

Those pages record decisions already made. Rewriting them changes the record without changing any decision. The test cases for #420 would build only the older pages that already meet the rules, so the other 19 stay untouched.
text
Should the after-build visual check also search the rendered page for "null" and "undefined"?
A
Yes, only where a row, line or box holds nothing but the word
Refuses a row, line or box that reads only "null" or "undefined". A sentence that mentions the word, as this page does, still builds.
B
Yes, the word anywhere on the page
Simpler, but it refuses this very page: I ran the search on this page: the word null appears 11 times, all inside quoted sentences.
C
No
The owed lists alone; nothing added to the visual check.

The owed lists only cover fields someone wrote down. The rendered-text search catches a field nobody listed, which is how the handoff plan's "null" got through. Matching only a part that is nothing but the word keeps pages that talk about it buildable.
strict
On a build plan page, which rows must list their files?
A
New and Changed rows
As issue #422 says; a Kept row changes nothing, so it has no files to list.
B
Every row, Kept ones too
Stricter, but a Kept row would have to list files it does not touch.
A file list says what a row will change. A Kept row by definition changes nothing.

wrapup.summary: The page builder refuses a page until everything that kind of page owes is filled in, and lists every missing item at once.
wrapup.changing: make_page.py gains the owed checks that apply to every page, plus those for proposal pages, build plan pages and QA pages; scripts/checks/make_page.py gains a test case for each.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the four choices and your approval of this design. The QA page step (#423) also waits for #389 to merge.
wrapup.next: A build plan page ("Build plan approved: page builder owed items") with the files and line estimates, then #420 to #424 built in order, each with its test cases first.
